item.title: An atavistic humanoid + a mysterious organization
item.description: An organization that believes that you can find humanity his glory in the past. It creates abnormal creatures. When the Foundation attacks one of their labs, they find my SCP to be the only life form left behind.
item.content:encoded:
Edit: Help please! I did something wrong I think, because there are 42 comments and the tread is locked.
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: I will tell most of the story trough addenda.

Elevator Pitch:
There is this organization who tries to recreate ancient creatures/gods trough genetic engineering.
When the Foundation attacks one of its labs, they find it to be destroyed, with most of the information taken. Except for one creature. My SCP. The core idea is this:

  • The SCP has treats of our ancestors (relatively low IQ, more hair etc).
  • The SCP can live for 25 years (the less years to live, the more heredity treats).
  • The SCP has the ability to mentally affect other live forms, although it can't do it on command
  • The SCP shows signs of affection towards a junior researcher
+ The story
- close this

The researchers didn't find something abnormal at first, so the security level was relatively low. Then, an attempt to murder the SCP was made. It failed, but the SCP should be contained at a safer location. While in transport to that location, the SCP attacks his guards and walks away. Foundation personal see the SCP, but they aren't alarmed (the third bullet list point, remember?). The SCP walks into the lunch room of the scientific department, and murders senior researcher ''insert name here''. After that, the involved Foundation personal are given a class E status, but are cleared for duty after intensive mental and psychic tests.

+ Reason for my SCP to do that
- I hope this makes sense

Wouldn't it be terrible, not knowing what is real and what is fake? And when you have been fooled so many times that you thought you couldn't be fooled anymore, and then someone you started seeing as a friend betrays you? Well that is what my SCP was thinking. The researcher it murdered was a spy for the organization, as is later discovered by the Foundation (she was the one to try and murder the SCP). My SCP recognized the voice, and thought that it was all just some sort of organization test. It leaves a note saying: ''I believed you'', where he is talking to the junior researcher from bullet list point 4.

Central Narrative:

+ The organization
- G'day! (: 

The idea is that there is an organization that tries to recreate gods/mythological creatures from the past trough genetic engineering. They try to create a leap-back in evolution, otherwise known as an atavism. Evolution is always positive, so reversing it should be mostly negative. That's why most of their attempts fail, or the creature dies at a young age. When the Foundation does an attack on one of its labs, they've already emptied it. Except for one: my SCP. They conduct, just like the Foundation, tests and contain the creatures safely.

+What the Foundation is going to do next 
- Thanks for reading by the way

Since the SCP is the only asset of information about the organization, it should be recovered as soon as possible, and not be killed. The Foundation found a series of text messages on the spy her laptop, talking about killing the SCP. The Foundation needs to find it, before they do.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The discovery of the SCP, that the senior researcher turns out to be a spy, and the relationship between the SCP and the junior researcher.

Additional Notes:
I really need to come up with some names.
Since the organization is about ancient creatures and science, would it make sense for them to speak Latin? I think it does and I can write in it. Let me know please!

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) A Young Reality Disruption
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Action

Elevator Pitch: A humanoid male that would accidentally warp-reality if he has too much stress or gets intensely outrageous.

Central Narrative:

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX is a reality-altering humanoid male that is approximately 2 feet tall. The subject will accidentally disrupt reality if mental capacities are large, resulting in a ZK-Class event occur. Their unstable emotions are the sources that can affect their power's capabilities, efficacy, and limitations.

SCP-XXXX was discovered when reports of a paranormal event have occurred, which is shown to be various vehicles falling from the skies, killing thousands of innocent lives. After this was brought to the Foundation, they've located all of the scene witnesses and wipe out their memories. Before doing so, they've asked the witnesses whether they know the cause of the phenomena. The civilians all said that they have no clue what the cause could be. The agents all know that who, or whatever could do so, is somewhere around in that area, as they've asked each people in the area until they've moved to the house of a high school male, which eventually claims that he is the cause of the phenomenon. After this, the Foundation has ordered the agents to lied to the boy's parents that he's going to school abroad.

In the interview, SCP-XXXX stated that he discovered his abilities when his father forces him to do a lot of work, which causes him a big amount of stress, also causes him to have a few mental stabilities problem1, and sometimes extremely aggressive, he would outburst.


Hook/Attention-Grabber: The high-school is a person who lives in a family with a very rigorous father. Due to seeing his son being too joyful and doesn't seem to care whether if he gets in trouble, the father always scolds him non-stop, slowly affecting his mental health.

Additional Notes:

Footnotes
1. Stated that he sometimes talks alone, play with his pencil, walks, run, and jumps around in circles while pulling his hair and talking alone at the same time.

item.title: Aerosol SCP
item.content:encoded:
Seeking green light: Yes

Page type: SCP Article

Page layout: Standard SCP format with several addendums and a link to an offset page.

Elevator pitch: The SCP is an anomalous aerosol created by the Manna Charitable Foundation with the intention of reducing the Earth's temperature to halt or reduce global warming by reflecting the Sun's rays using anomalously enhanced sulfur dioxide which are designed to last longer and grow even larger by abosrbing Co2 in the atmosphere. The conprocs for the first iteration states that its currently uncontained and personal assigned are to work on either containing it or lessen its negative effects, as well as preventing the public from learning its anomalous effects.

In the second iteration, the conprocs states its the cause of an active GK-Class "Ozone destruction" scenario and while they are working on to stop by spreading alkaline all across the atmosphere, their unsure if it'll work or not due to the magnitude of the SCP.

Central narrative: A long time ago, the MCF was working on Project Sunna to try and fix global warming as its directly/indirectly responsible for a lot of bad things happening in the world, with funding from not only some governments but also anomaloud GoIs. Its the biggest project MCF has created.

They then released it via planes into the atmosphere which worked for a while; however, as years gone by, the ozone became severely damaged in some parts of the world to the point where thousands are dying. As the SCP Foundation is trying to stop it, the MCF however have fallen and received a shit ton of backlash for this.

Hook: While it maybe another one of those MCF articles where they try to do good things, only to end in disaster this one however takes it to another, global scale where the MCF really fucked up.

Notes: I need someone to help fact check these things to make sure if at least some of it correct.

item.title: "Man of None"
item.description: Anyone who acknowledges a relationship between the man and themselves dies painfully within 24 hours.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre (Optional): Horror / Drama / Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): It'll begin as a standardized SCP document, listing the object class, containment procedures, etc etc. The bulk of the article, however, will be inside of the addendum - the interviews, more specifically.

Elevator Pitch: A man under the affect of a seeming "curse". Anyone who verbally confirms any relationship between them and the man dies within the next 24 hours in an unspeakably horrific way, varying from person to person.

Central Narrative: Man of None", a concept I had for an SCP, is a seemingly regular man with a personal love for technology. However, what is strange is the fact anyone who verbally recognizes a relationship between the speaker and the object are killed within 24 hours in an unspeakably painful way. While this may seem as if it's simply for the shock factor of gore and horrific deaths, there's a much darker thing behind it.
He wants to die, however due to the nature of the SCP Foundation his death would be something which would not be wanted. So, they contain him and give him psychological treatment (of course on a very strict regiment), however it never helps. With plenty of research, the only way which suicide patients are helped is via forming relationships with those who help them. And, any relationship with him causes horrific death. So, he's left alone in the world. All that people will call him is an object. They will not say he's their "friend". Not a "loved one". "Family", "enemy", any of the sort is never heard from them.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The man, due to irrelevant trauma, has developed [REDACTED] disorder - which, with hints throughout the article, would be Borderline Personality Disorder. He is absolutely desperate for some form of recognition, approval, or relationship between another human. However, due to the nature of his "curse", he's unable to. This plays to one of the largest human fears of being truly alone. He goes through phases of being desperate for someone to tell him that they care for him in some form, and phases of attempting to hide from others so they don't die a horrific death. He's seen numerous of the things which he's caused, which leaves a permanent trauma to him.

Additional Notes: I'm horrific when it comes to formatting first of all, so if I've messed this up please tell me. I'd like criticism on the entire thing really.

item.title: SCP Idea Seeks Greenlight
item.description: A doll wants you to worship it, a little at a time.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

  • Doll of a non-descript female anime figure
  • Causes those nearby to into a near-worship state
  • Demands paltry tribute to stay sated
  • The character is unable to be described, named, nor the anime she is from
  • Individuals under the effect feel compelled to talk about her, discussing objective traits like beauty, coolness, etc.
  • When asked, individuals under the effect will reflect questions such as 'YOU don't know HER?' 'I can't believe you'd have to ask me that; a REAL fan would know.'
  • The doll manifested due to a natural proclivity for 'otaku' obsession.
  • The doll represents a void of concept, it can never be fully filled as an idea, so it seeks material items to sate itself.
  • The student discovered the figure and gradually became a classic case of neglecting himself in favor of the idol, pushing people away while lording over them how great his new obsession was.

Central Narrative:

The doll exists in such a way that it compels those nearby to give it small tokens, with no discernable pattern as to what that item needs to be. It prefers to be above eye level on a shelf. The doll was found in a college dorm closet whose occupant began failing out due to offering term papers and other collegiate supplies. Initially thinking that the student was a hoarder, not much thought was given to the situation until the closet was forcefully cleaned and the student's roommate was found bound, malnourished, and near-death within the mass, assumed to be given as tribute when the student did not have anything else to give.

To remain generally inert, the item must receive a tribute every 2-3 days. However, a note from Foundation management has requested that office supplies no longer be offered due to the supply closet constantly needing to be restocked. The longer the doll goes without tribute, the stronger its pull.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
The doll possesses both memetic and antimemetic properties, compelling those under its effect to want to talk about her all the time but unable to physically describe any aspect that would give her characterization.

item.title: A genetics enhancement lab

item.content:encoded:

Genre (Optional): Creepy

Elevator Pitch: The SCP itself is just a glass cage. When you put a specimen inside it, it "reverts" to a single-celled egg, allowing for genetic modification. It will then grow back to the same specimen, but hundreds of generations later, accounting for the modifications brought to it (or not, if there wasn't any).

Central Narrative: The story is based around a doctor and her researcher who tries to understand the SCP, but more importantly what the previous owner was trying to do with it, and what happened to him.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The SCP revolves around damaged notes from the previous owner, describing a few of his experiments, and his downfall. Of course, most of the notes are missing.

Additional Notes: I have written a rough sandbox of it because it's been on my mind for a while, even though it is far from finished. I come back to it and bring changes to it a lot, if you'd like to read it.

item.title: The Mother
item.description: (260 Words) A line of anomalous women all related, when one gives birth, it dies.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article, Tale, GoI Format, Joke SCP, Site Dossier, Other (specify) : SCP Article.

Elevator Pitch:
A single branch of anomalous female humanoid creatures dating back to 150 AD. The creature she births brings a new anomalous effect. This effect is non-voluntary, and takes place whenever a criteria is met. This SCP grows at a rate similar to a human being, but once reaching the year of 29, regardless of contact with any males or injections, she will begin to experience the stages of child birth at a rapid pace, giving birth 3 hours later, and self-terminating. Each generation is only female, and contains one or more anomalous power.

Central Narrative:
A linear narrative; The capture of the SCP, attempts to contain each generation, attempts to try to stop the birth process, attempted force abortions, subsequent failures, attemps at containing the 'reincarnations' of this SCP as they come, and the learning of how this SCP functions on a deeper level.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
Each female born from this line carries one or more strong anomalous powers, such as the ability to create and snuff out fires, the ability to warp reality, or the ability to instantly terminate any creature that is in it's area when angry. The seemingly randomness of anomalous power after birth leaving to a constant struggle in contain each generation, and changing of the classification of the SCP. This SCP is only one familial line, not expanding out towards other families.

Additional Notes:
Article will contain multiple tabs that each have their own interviews, tests, and trials done on the SCP, leaving it open for infinite possibilities. I do not know how to do this yet, but would like some ideas on where to look to do this.

item.title: The Spire - needs greenlights
item.content:encoded:
It's a chemically changing rock. Name is work in progress, and I'm not too happy with the discovery, so any help/suggestions would be nice

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror/intriguing?

Page Layout (Optional): Standard article. After description, will go over discovery, and after discovery will then go over test logs.

Elevator Pitch: It's a tall rock that slightly twists. The tip of it will be called element A, and the base of it will be called element B. If an object touches the tip, element A changes into the majority of the atoms in that object. There are various things that cause a teleport event, but when that happens, the spire disappears and reappears at a random spot on the earth. element B then becomes the old element A, element A becomes the closest solid element near the tip, and the spire absorbs every current element B atom in a 1km radius.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: It was discovered when a redacted reality bender started rampaging, and along with various other items it created the spire. Some clean up MTF member accidentally touches the tip with his glove, and his glove disappears along with the spire. It's found in some town where around half of the people there dropped dead and withered on the spot, because the glove was mostly carbon, and all the carbon was stolen from their bodies. The spire is found in the town, and it's got a carbon base with a solid oxygen tip (from the oxygen in the granite that built the town)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The rules for the spire are pretty strict, so it's like a constant reminder that whatever the old tip was, all those atoms could immediately disappear in the center of a city, but it could also appear in the center of a forest, and be difficult to track down, so I feel that would draw people into the story. Also there's a mention near the beginning about testing being discontinued, so I feel people would want to see why

Additional Notes: The things that cause a teleportation event(work in progress name) are: The tip is touched with the same majority atom as the tip already had, so instead of staying the same it teleports. 108 hours pass without a tip change. If the tip is a radioactive element, the moment an atom in it decays, it undergoes the event (which is pretty much instantly). If the tip and base are the same element, it undergoes the event. If the tip is helium, it undergoes the event. I can explain more, as a lot of the info had to be cut down due to size limit.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: HOT SIRENS IN YOUR AREA - Greenlights needed!
item.description: A coven of sirens- yes, like the mythological Greek kind-
item.content:encoded:
A coven of sirens- yes, like the mythological Greek kind- find themselves adapting to the modern climate in order to seek their prey.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre: Comedy, mainly, but not in an un-serious manner.

Elevator Pitch: You know those clearly fake ads you get on nsfw websites? The ones that’re like “HOT SINGLES IN YOUR AREA”, et cetera. Yeah. Those, but anomalous, and set up by Sirens, as in the type that’d lure sailors to death. The ad, if loaded on a page, would display a message along the lines of “10 HOT (xyz) WITHIN (distance)! TEXT NOW!”

+ show block
– hide block

As time went by, the distance would gradually decrease, and the number increase. This would culminate in the subject being ambushed, and then… well, consumed, by a number of horrible, vaguely humanoid fishy-people.

The Foundation would later track these ads to a certain location, and, unable to block the ads via webcrawlers or other non-anomalous means, would send in an MTF team to find out what’s going on. There’s an exploration log, and the anomaly is accidentally neutralised when the coven of sirens panics upon realising there’s angry fellows with guns in the hideout and collapses the building in order to escape, breaking all of their paratech that let them make and maintain the anomalous ads in the first place.

Central Narrative: The context behind this strange new manner of Greek monsters luring in prey is simply that people don’t usually fall for the ole’ “Sing to the sailors until they follow you and drown” trick, and they’ve had to resort to new and unusual means of tracking targets. Inkeeping with the tradition of luring sailors in with beautiful songs and false faces, they decide to essentially hijack NSFW spam ads, which ends up working pretty well.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: As far as I’m aware, nobody’s done sirens as an SCP before, and beyond that, the concept of the fake ads on the sides of sketchy sites actually being dangerous beyond just giving your computer malware is a little spine-chilling. And also really funny, when you think about it.

Additional Notes: As this would be my first SCP, essentially any critique at all would be greatly appreciated.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts and properly space your paragraphs. ~Zyn

item.title: "When We Didn't Dream" - An SCP Tale Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
A troublesome teenager utilizes mysterious livestock to control his dreams. A tale about SCP-1498.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: Tale

This tale doesn't take place in The Foundation itself. It's based around one specific SCP before it was contained.

Elevator Pitch: A teenager by the name of Ty encounters SCP-1498 in the woods, and begins to abuse its abilities. However, when he slowly starts to become an instance of SCP-1498, he struggles to find help. This takes place a month before SCP-1498's original containment date.

Central Narrative: Taking place in august of 1965, just before SCP-1498 (which this tale is about) is contained, a troublesome teenager, Ty, stumbles across SCP-1498 in the woods and learns that he can order dreams from the SCP. He begins to abuse the ability, spending most of his time asleep, dreaming. However, when his body begins to slowly turn into instances of the SCP, he attempts to find "The Oneiroi Collective" (the people who possibly designed the SCP) to help him. However, upon searching phone books, he discovers that the phone number to call them only exists on the instances of SCP-1498. He hurries back to where he last saw them, but they've vanished completely. Luckily, a phone wire that goes through the woods leads him to an abandoned office building, where he finds the livestock entering. Ty catches up to them, managing to get on the phone with The Oneiroi Collective. However, it's too late, and Ty completely transforms into an instance of SCP-1498-1, mindlessly wandering back into the woods, ironically dreaming of the days when he didn't dream at all.

Hook/Attention Grabber: The realization that Ty basically has no way out of the situation he's in. This is the foundation of most of the tension throughout the tale, as it will seem almost completely hopeless. Which, by the end, it's revealed that it was, indeed, hopeless. At least, that's the goal I'll try to achieve with this tale.

Additional Notes: Obviously, this is a rough outline of what happens, and it will almost certainly change (hopefully for the better) if this gets greenlighted. I'm also not the author of SCP-1498, and as so tried to keep this story as distant from the lore set up in the SCP itself.

Here's a link to SCP-1498, which this tale is based on: http://www.scpwiki.com/scp-1498

item.title: Bearer of Bad News
item.description: This SCP would be a British man who appears to random individuals, giving them bad news of various severity.
item.content:encoded:

The central narrative would be told over the testing logs, a baseline test to see how it works before certain "interesting" tests are done, the story here would be subtle in the notes afterwards, subjects reporting feeling safer after a certain death, etc.

The testing logs will include what I believe to be unique testing logs, like what would happen if someone put their name in for both options, what would happen if the distance was set at a giant amount, etc.
